newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia opposition says protests set to continue.
newsitem.headline: Serbia opposition says protests set to continue.

text.p: One of Serbia's main opposition parties said on Friday it would continue street protests despite the government's acknowledgement that some local elections had been won by its opponents.

Earlier, a letter from Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic to the Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) acknowledged that opposition won nine municipalities in Belgrade in November 17 local elections but did not acknowledge its victory in other big towns.

Democratic Party leader Zoran Djindjic told Reuters: "The letter is a clear rejection of OSCE recommendations. We cannot accept partial solutions and we are continuing our peaceful demonstrations to attain our goal -- recognition of our complete victory at the November 17 local elections."

Vuk Draskovic, leader of the Serbian Renewal Movement, which together with the Democratic Party and Civil Alliance comprises the Zajedno opposition coalition, denounced Milutinovic's response as lies and a rejection of OSCE recommendations.
In his letter, Milutinovic said the "coalition 'Zajedno' won the majority of votes in nine municipalities in Belgrade".
Milutinovic also said the authorities still needed more detail to clarify results in others towns.

The letter was sent as a response to an OSCE report by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez who led a mission to Serbia to investigate the disputed elections. The OSCE acknowledged Zajedno victory in 15 biggest cities in Serbia, including Belgrade.
